cases.description: git reset --hard, snake dialect (Claude/Codex), denies with the reset-hard kind named.
git reset --hard, Copilot bash with a JSON-string toolArgs, denies.
git reset --hard, Copilot powershell with a JSON-string toolArgs, denies.
git clean -fd (combined short cluster), snake dialect, denies.
git clean --force, Copilot bash, denies.
git clean -xdf (combined short cluster), Copilot powershell, denies.
git push --force, snake dialect, denies.
git push -f, Copilot bash, denies.
git push --force-with-lease, Copilot powershell, denies.
git checkout ., snake dialect, denies.
git checkout -- <path>, Copilot bash, denies.
git restore <path>, Copilot powershell, denies.
git push --force-if-includes=<value>, the =value form, still denies.
git restore --staged --worktree <path> touches the worktree too, so it denies (resolves the --staged/--worktree ambiguity the spec flags).
git checkout -f main discards local modifications; -f is the explicit force flag that makes an otherwise-excluded branch checkout destructive.
git checkout --force main, the long form of the same force flag, denies.
Bare git checkout -f (no target) still discards local modifications.
git switch -f main discards local modifications the same way checkout -f does.
git switch --discard-changes main, the long form of switch's force flag, denies.
git push -uf origin feature force-pushes via a combined short-flag cluster; push's force detection is cluster-aware the same way clean's is.
git push origin +main is git's own force-push spelling, no flag required.
git push origin +HEAD:main, the same leading-plus refspec form with a source:dest pair, denies.
git --work-tree=. reset --hard: an unrecognized but self-contained (=value) global option no longer breaks subcommand detection.
git --no-pager reset --hard: an unrecognized global option that takes no value is skipped by itself.
git -C. reset --hard: -C with its value attached (no space) is self-contained, which real git also accepts.
git -C /repo reset --hard: -C's value in a separate token is consumed as a pair; pre-existing behavior with no prior coverage.
ENV=1 git push --force: a leading VAR=value assignment is stripped before classification; pre-existing behavior with no prior coverage.
command git clean -fd: a leading literal `command` is stripped before classification; pre-existing behavior with no prior coverage.
git push --mirror force-updates every remote ref and propagates deletions, a forced rewrite of remote history by any reading; denies as force-push.
Git reset --hard (capitalized executable, valid on Copilot's powershell tool) is recognized case-insensitively and denies the same as lowercase.
GIT reset --hard (all-caps executable) is recognized case-insensitively and denies the same as lowercase.
git.exe reset --hard (the Windows executable spelling) is recognized and denies the same as bare git.

/usr/bin/git reset --hard still allows: the case-insensitive/`.exe` fix is about the bare executable name's spelling, not about resolving paths, so a full path stays an accepted false negative (see header).
Plain git push with no force flag is not destructive; yeet needs it.
git push --delete origin foo removes a named ref rather than rewriting history, so it sits outside the closed set this hook's standing rule enumerates (see header's accepted-exclusions list).
git clean with no force flag allows.
git clean -fd -n is a dry run; -n suppresses the match.
git clean -fdn is a dry run with -n inside the same combined cluster as the force flag; dry-run suppression is cluster-aware, symmetric with force detection.
git push --force --dry-run never actually pushes; --dry-run suppresses the match.
git stash is out of scope: the standing rule scopes it by "work you don't own", unobservable from the command text.
git stash pop is out of scope, same reasoning as plain stash.
git stash drop is out of scope, same reasoning as plain stash.
git stash clear is out of scope, same reasoning as plain stash.
git rebase is destructive only against shared history, unobservable from the command text, and routine locally.
git commit --amend is out of scope, same reasoning as rebase.
git branch -D is reflog-recoverable and not in the standing rule's scope.
git restore --staged <path> alone unstages but never touches the worktree.
git checkout <branchname> is branch checkout, not a worktree discard; accepted false negative.
git checkout -b <name> creates a branch; not a worktree discard.
git switch <branchname> with no force flag is a plain branch switch, not a worktree discard.
git push -un origin feature: a combined short-flag cluster with unrelated letters but no 'f' must not match (the inverse of the force-cluster fix).
git push origin "+weird": the tokenizer keeps quote characters as part of the token, so a quoted leading + is not mistaken for the force-push refspec form.
git --git-dir .git reset --hard: the two-token form of an unrecognized global option (value in a separate token) is an accepted false negative, documented in the header.
bash -c "git reset --hard" is indirection; accepted false negative.
/usr/bin/git reset --hard is a full-path invocation; accepted false negative.
env git reset --hard is indirection via env; accepted false negative.
echo $(git reset --hard) buries the command in a substitution; accepted false negative.
--help on a destructive form suppresses the match, same exclusion detectOutwardMutations applies.
-h on a destructive form suppresses the match too.
A quoted commit message mentioning a blocked form must not trip the classifier: the tokenizer sees git commit, not git reset.
A heredoc body mentioning a blocked form is stripped before classification.
A shell comment mentioning a blocked form is stripped before classification.
The tokenizer splits on &&, so a blocked form later in a compound command still denies.

Two same-kind occurrences land well inside the racing-loser window (this runner's own back-to-back subprocess spawns take single-digit milliseconds, far under the 2000ms threshold ported from plan-gate.js), so both deny: a fast retry is indistinguishable from a same-turn race and is treated the same way. The companion case immediately below (same-kind-twice-backdated-second-allows) back-dates the marker past RACE_MS to prove the other side: a genuine model-turn-later retry passes.

Companion to same-kind-twice-fast-both-deny: the second occurrence's marker is back-dated past RACE_MS (2000ms) before it runs, so this call sees a genuine model-turn-later retry rather than a race, and passes. This is deny-once's headline behavior and had no automated coverage before backdateMarkersMs existed.

reset-hard is gated and its marker is back-dated, then a compound command matching both reset-hard and force-push runs: reset-hard is already-seen (allowed silently for that kind) while force-push is new, so the deny names only force-push, not reset-hard.

Warn-path counterpart to same-kind-twice-backdated-second-allows: GITGUARD_WARN=1 with a back-dated marker means the second occurrence emits nothing (a genuine retry) rather than warning again, mirroring the deny-mode retry-passes case on the warn path.

Back-dating reset-hard's marker must not leak into force-push's own freshness: force-push's first occurrence still denies as new (unaffected by the unrelated back-date), and an immediate same-kind repeat right after still races and denies, proving force-push's marker was never touched by the earlier reset-hard-only back-date.
Two distinct kinds in one session each deny on their own first occurrence.
GITGUARD_DISABLED=1 allows a command that would otherwise deny.
GITGUARD_WARN=1 demotes deny to a non-blocking warning on the snake dialect.

GITGUARD_WARN=1: a second call of the same kind, landing inside the racing-loser window like same-kind-twice-fast-both-deny, warns again rather than silently allowing, proving warn mode is governed by the same race-protected marker claim as deny mode (not a separate path the fix missed).
GITGUARD_WARN=1 on Copilot has no soft-warn channel, so it degrades to allow plus a stderr note.
GITGUARD_DISABLED=1 and GITGUARD_WARN=1 set together: disabled wins, full allow.
Empty stdin parses as {} and allows silently.
Unparseable stdin hits the top-level catch and emits an explicit allow, regardless of dialect.
A Bash tool_input with no command field has nothing to classify, so it allows silently.
A non-Bash tool on the snake dialect (Read) allows silently.
A non-bash/powershell Copilot tool (view) allows explicitly.
A Copilot toolArgs that already arrives as an object (not a JSON string) is tolerated and still classified.
git add .env stages a bare .env file, denies as stage-env-file.
git add config/.env.production, a nested path with a non-template suffix, denies by basename.
git commit .env -m "wip" names .env directly on a commit invocation: stage-env-file is now scoped to add only, a documented accepted false negative, so this allows.
git commit -m "add .env to .gitignore" is an ordinary commit message whose interior word matches .env; scoping stage-env-file to add only removes the surface that misread it as a pathspec.

git commit -n .env -m "wip": on commit, -n means --no-verify, not dry-run, which the pre-dispatch -n suppression used to misread; scoping stage-env-file to add only removes the gated surface entirely, so this allows (documented accepted false negative, same as the commit-pathspec gap).
git add -A .env.local: a non-template suffix behind an unrelated -A flag still denies.
git add .env.example is the conventionally-committed template suffix; allows.
git add .env.sample is a conventionally-committed template suffix; allows.
git add src/env.js does not match the .env pattern (no leading dot); allows.
git add environment.ts merely contains "env" and does not match; allows.
git commit -m "wip" with no path argument has nothing to classify; allows.
git add . is a bare sweep with no explicit path; the hook can't see what it would stage, accepted false negative.
git add --dry-run .env: the existing --dry-run suppression (checked before subcommand dispatch) applies to stage-env-file too.
git add ".env": shellWords strips the surrounding double quotes before the basename check, so a quoted .env still denies.
git add '.env': shellWords strips the surrounding single quotes before the basename check, so a quoted .env still denies.

git add .\env: shellWords unescapes \e to a literal e the same way a real shell does, handing the basename check .env, so this now denies (previously an accepted false negative under the old token-preserving tokenizer).
git add .env.defaults is the dotenv-defaults conventionally-committed template suffix; allows.

Regression for fix 3 (per-file marker keying): git add .env.test denies and its marker is backdated past the race window so the retry of .env.test allows (a genuine model-turn-later retry of THAT file), but a subsequent git add .env in the SAME session still denies, since one file's confirmation must not disarm the guard for a different file.

Regression for fix 1 (full-path marker keying, not basename): git add config/.env denies and its marker is backdated past the race window so the retry of config/.env allows (a genuine model-turn-later retry of THAT path), but a subsequent git add other/.env in the SAME session still denies, since two different directories sharing a basename must not share a marker.

Regression for fix 2 (shellWords word splitting): git add "config dir/.env" is one quoted pathspec containing whitespace, which the whitespace split at the top of detectDestructiveGit breaks into two tokens before shellWords repairs it; denies.
git add "config/.env": a quoted nested path with no interior whitespace, still denies via shellWords's quote-stripping.
Regression for fix A: git add .e"nv" has a quote appearing mid-word rather than at the token's start, so any check keyed on a token-initial quote misses it; shellWords catches it and denies.
Regression for fix A: git add config/".env" wraps only the basename in quotes, mid-token, not the whole word; shellWords catches it and denies.

Regression for fix C: git add .ENV denies and its marker is backdated past the race window so the retry of .ENV allows, but a subsequent git add .env in the SAME session (a different file on a case-sensitive filesystem) still denies, since the composite marker key must preserve exact case rather than collapsing both onto one lowercased marker.

Regression for fix B: an env-only git add .env deny should not carry the generic protect-the-working-tree retry line, which is the wrong (bypass-coaching) instruction for a disclosure risk; only the secrets-specific rationale and its own retry instruction should be present. expectExcludes is the negative-assertion mechanism this runner supports; there is no mechanism here to assert the generic RULE SENTENCE itself is absent beyond this exact retry-instruction string, so that stronger claim is not mechanically covered by this fixture.

expectExcludes: Confirm the user asked for this exact operation

cases.description: A Copilot toolArgs that is neither a string nor an object (e.g. a number) has no command to extract, so it allows.
